Consultants to Westmoreland Resources have monitored chemical quality of Sarpy and East Fork of Sarpy Creeks since October, 1972. Their reports describe the water as predominantly magnesium and calcium sulfate type and containing 2,000 to 4,000 mg/l of dissolved solids, depending on the time of year and amount of runoff present. pH ranges from 7.9 to 8.4.
Data on the chemical characteristics of Tullock Creek and its tributaties are few. In general, the specific conductivity, calculated dissolved solids, calcium, magnesium, bicarbonate, and sulfate concentrations are higher for Sarpy Creek. Results of trace metals analyzed for both creeks are about the same. Laboratory turbidity and total suspended solids are noticeably higher for the Tullock Creek stations. Because the geology, soil types, land use, and precipitation type and frequency are relatively similar in the Tullock Creek and Sarpy Creek basins, one might expect the type of waters found in Sarpy Creek areas to be indicative of the type of water to be found in Tullock Creek.

Data are too few, however, to completely accept this assumption. A description of Westmoreland Resource's surface water monitoring systems, a summary of results to date, and data tables are presented in Appendix D.
